turn1.explanation: The unit fires most strongly on bird-name tokens, whatever the word means in context: real birds (sparrow, owls), surnames (Finch, Swan, Heron, Falcon), idioms (lame duck, green swan), bands (Flamingos), code identifiers (Kestrel) and even the acronym SWAN. A separate, weaker response appears on abbreviated month names in dates (Sep, Oct, Nov, Aug, Feb, Sept).
turn1.evidence: Every top example (activation 8-10) is a bird word in a non-bird sense as often as a literal one, so the unit tracks the word form, not the animal. All mid-range examples (5-7) are month abbreviations, which have no evident semantic or orthographic link to birds.
turn1.missing_data: Activations on month abbreviations in more contexts and on other short capitalized abbreviations would show whether the date response is a real second feature or part of a broader token-shape pattern.
